newsitem.title: USA: Lucent Technologies sued over trademark.
newsitem.headline: Lucent Technologies sued over trademark.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc was sued Thursday for alleged trademark infringement in U.S. District Court in Delaware.

In court papers Lucent Information Management Inc of Bala Cynwyd, Pa., alleged that Lucent Technologies knew the "Lucent" trademark had already been adopted but decided not to be "inconvenienced" by a similarly named small company without an "established" identity.

Lucent Technologies was first incorporated as NS-MPG Inc to carry on portions of the business once conducted by AT&T and adopted the Lucent name in November, 1995. According to court papers, Lucent spent $50 million on its initial advertising budget to convince "the public that it was the only company in the U.S. using the name Lucent' for...telecommunication and information systems".

Lucent Information said in its lawsuit that the name Lucent Technologies is creating "confusion in the marketplace" that interferes with Lucent Information's mission to create an electronic office filing system.
Lucent Information is seeking unspecified compensatory, real and punitive damages for alleged tradename infringement and unfair competition.
A Lucent Technologies spokesman could not be reached for comment.
